title: Nia and the Sunbeam Juice
markdown:
The Sunbeam Festival filled Willow Creek with soft music and glowing lanterns. Nia the gardener loved it, especially the ruby-red festival juice that tasted like warm sunshine. She filled a tall jug with care.

“Oh, Wisp,” she whispered to her fluffy cat, already asleep in a sunbeam. “I wonder if the juice will still be sparkly when the festival is over and the days grow warm.”

Wisp twitched an ear, as if to say, worry not.

The next morning a pale blue sky. Nia tiptoed to the jug, ready for a sip. When she tilted it, the juice did not slosh. Unyielding and cool, like a river stone.

“Wisp! Wake up, my dear.” Wisp stretched, padded over, blinked, and nudged the jug. A muffled sound.

Dr. Sol ambled by, kind eyes, and peered at Nia’s puzzled face. “Well now. Look what the cold night and the morning sun have been doing.” He pointed. “When liquids like our juice stay very, very cold for a long time, they can turn solid, like ice. When the warm gentle sun shines, they begin to remember they are liquids again. Watch.”

A tiny ruby-red droplet appeared at the rim and slowly slid down the cool glass.

Nia’s eyes widened. Not magic. Warmth. “The sun is changing the juice so we can drink it again.”

Dr. Sol smiled. “The sun’s warmth helps solids — juice that went like ice — become liquids once more.”

They scooped the slowly melting juice into small cool bowls. Nia and Wisp shared, a cool sweet refreshment. Other friends came, marvelling at the treat that had transformed because the night had been cold enough, and the morning kind enough.

Dr. Sol did not turn it into a list of all the world’s water. Nia nodded. Wisp’s whiskers were lightly dusted ruby red. The jug, softening in the sunbeam, gave another drop, then another, until there was enough for sipping and no more need to tilt a stone.
